mathematical_facts: Swapping byte values between c0 and c1 leaves their XOR difference unchanged on every swapped coordinate: c0'[i]^c1'[i] = c1[i]^c0[i] = c0[i]^c1[i]. Hence c0'^c1' = c0^c1.

With SBOX=id the cipher is affine: E(p)=M_r p+k_E, D(c)=M_r^-1 c+k_D with D the exact inverse of E. Therefore q0^q1 = M_r^-1 (c0'^c1') = M_r^-1 (c0^c1) = p0^p1 for EVERY r, EVERY S, EVERY key. The harness pair-difference trial map in the affine limit is the IDENTITY.
The worker rejects zero word-diffs, so every nontrivial trial has p0^p1 nonzero on exactly the active PW words; the instrument's W = 4-|A| on every nontrivial trial, independent of r and S.

The swap perturbation KEEPS the swapped bytes: c0' = c0 + Z_keep (c0^c1), so the one-sided yoyo difference is q0^p0 = M_r^-1 Z_keep M_r d, with Z_keep the mask that keeps CW[S] (zeroes the complement).

The record's operator Z_{CW[S]} ZEROES the swapped words (record object text), which is the complement mask: the record's T = M_r^-1 Z_zero M_r equals neither the harness pair difference (identity) nor the one-sided perturbation (Z_keep). Note T_zero + T_keep = I (the two masks sum to identity).
